A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same survey and contain readable text, equations, six figures, and ten tables. All pages were checked; neither version contains a separate appendix, and both end with references.

before.justification: v1 presents formal preliminaries, taxonomies, and literature catalogues. Reported performance outcomes are attributed to cited studies; no original empirical study is reported.

after.justification: v2 remains a literature survey. Its additions, including Section 6.4, summarize cited research and introduce no original experimental or data-analysis results.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes an implemented algorithm or model. Revisions concern the conceptual formalization and descriptions of surveyed methods, without establishing a changed procedure developed by this work.

E1.justification: Table 9 revises the benchmark catalogue, including adding WindowsAgentArena, SMAC-Hard, and TacticCraft. These are literature listings; neither version actually uses datasets or environments for its own training or evaluation.

E2.justification: Additions such as LitePPO in Table 2 and UI-TARS-2 in Table 7 expand descriptive catalogues. Neither version evaluates a proposed system against a set of baselines.

E3.justification: Neither version conducts an evaluation with its own splits, metrics, budgets, or testing procedures. Revised descriptions of cited systems do not establish a changed evaluation protocol for this survey.

E4.justification: No original ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity studies, or case studies are added or removed. The new mechanistic discussion synthesizes analyses attributed to other studies.

E5.justification: No repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-reporting procedures are introduced or revised. The added pass@k discussion reports findings from cited literature.

E6.justification: Secondary result reporting changes: Section 4.2.1 removes v1's DeepCoder-14B claim of +8% Pass@1 gains and 60.6% on LiveCodeBench. v2 also adds qualitative findings about smaller RL-trained MLE agents and competing pass@k trends in Section 6.4. These are changes to cited findings, not new results produced by the survey.

T1.justification: Section 2.3 adds a recursive action-space description allowing an action to represent a sequence of primitive actions, and replaces 'disjoint components' with 'distinct subspaces.' Equation 1 also makes the discount factor of 1 explicit. The remaining formalization and objectives are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statement, and conclusion retain the same claims: an MDP/POMDP conceptual distinction, a capability-and-task taxonomy, and a practical resource compendium emphasizing RL's role in adaptive agent behavior.

C2.justification: New Section 6.4 contrasts amplification of existing capabilities with acquisition of new capabilities and explicitly leaves the mechanism unresolved. Section 4.2.3 also removes the categorical claim that RL uniquely captures long-term decision-making skills unavailable through static supervised training.

D1.justification: Table 10 adds repository links for RL-Factory, ROLL, VerlTool, AgentRL, and Oat, with accompanying framework descriptions. Table 9 removes the direct HumanEval and MBPP repository listings. The survey's own repository link remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 extends existing coverage with works on compute allocation for planning, memory management and latent memory, agent frameworks, and the mechanistic debate. Figure 2 gains attribution to Kumar et al. The central research positioning remains intact; reference deduplication and publication updates do not constitute removal of the corresponding works.

P1.justification: v2 reorders the introductory literature paragraphs, revises passages in Sections 2.3, 3.1, and 4.2, adds Section 6.4, and updates the author list. These are targeted edits within the retained seven-section organization.

P2.justification: Several tables gain or lose catalogue rows, Table 3 adds gray highlighting, and Table 5 moves Posterior-GRPO and Policy Filtration into the code-generation group. Figure 2 changes colors and legend styling and expands its caption. The overall figure and table design remains recognizable.

improvement.justification: Updated literature and resource links improve the survey's usefulness, while Section 6.4 adds a more balanced treatment of capability claims and Section 2.3 clarifies composite actions. These are useful refinements to the existing synthesis. Some additions remain under-edited, notably the blank fields in Table 9's new WindowsAgentArena row, limiting the overall gain.
